examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
examples.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following identity: 

$$
1= \csc^2{\theta} -\cot^2{\theta}
$$

Substituting the above identity into the given expression, and then factoring it as a difference of squares, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )\,\cancel{(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )}}{\cancel{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }}+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =(\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta )+\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $({cot}^{2}⁡x+1)^{2}-2{csc}^{2}⁡x+1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the identities

$$
{cot}^{2}⁡x+1={csc}^{2}⁡x,\,{csc}^{2}⁡x-1={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Then, we simplify our expression using the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({cot}^{2}⁡x+1)^{2}-2{csc}^{2}⁡x+1 & =({csc}^{2}⁡x)^{2}-2\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡x\cdot 1+{1}^{2} \\  & =({csc}^{2}⁡x-1)^{2} \\  & =({cot}^{2}⁡x)^{2} \\  & ={cot}^{4}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$
